feed.title: Ted Tschopp's AI News
feed.subtitle: Latest AI News and Ratings from Ted Tschopp

entry.title: Codex for every role, tool, and workflow [ ! ]
entry.summary: OpenAI's Codex release packages role-specific apps, skills, instructions, and workflows so teams can apply AI coding agents across functions like data analytics, sales, and creative production. The deeper insight is that reusable AI skills may become a new market-based layer for organizing work, with Codex pointing toward modular, tradable, and increasingly standardized agent capabilities.

entry.title: The Next Era of Knowledge Work [ * ]
entry.summary: OpenAI's report frames knowledge work as a set of fragmented workflows across tabs, tools, and data silos, with Codex increasingly being used beyond traditional software engineering. Our analysts found that the biggest AI productivity opportunity may lie with non-technical employees, whose digital and highly verifiable tasks are well-suited for automation by emerging Codex-like agents.

entry.title: Rethinking Search as Code Generation [ * ]
entry.summary: Perplexity's research reimagines search as agent-generated code that can orchestrate retrieval, ranking, filtering, fan-out, and tool use in a more structured sandbox. Our analysts highlighted this as important because the pattern reduces probabilistic tool-calling loops, cuts token usage, and offers a reusable architecture for agentic search beyond Perplexity itself.

entry.title: How Rippling Went AI-Native Across Every Product in 6 Months with Deep Agents and LangSmith [ * ]
entry.summary: LangChain's case study describes how Rippling built a production AI layer across HR, IT, payroll, finance, and global operations using supervising agents, specialized sub-agents, and LangSmith observability. The useful takeaway is the emphasis on context engineering and production agent orchestration, though our analysts noted that the article was stronger on what Rippling built than on detailed implementation mechanics.

entry.title: The Next Frontier of Visual AI Is Code [ ~ ]
entry.summary: a16z argues that visual AI is moving from pure diffusion-based generation toward code-based artifacts such as SVG, HTML, CSS, and React components that are easier to edit and preserve. The main insight is that structured visual representations make AI-generated images and interfaces more controllable, but our analysts saw the piece as more of a venture thesis than an enterprise case study with hard adoption or ROI data.

entry.title: Building a hill-climbing machine: Launching seven new MAI models [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Microsoft's announcement introduces seven MAI models, including reasoning, coding, image, transcription, and frontier-tuning capabilities, alongside a Mayo Clinic healthcare-model collaboration. Our analysts viewed this as optional because it is largely a product announcement, with the bigger takeaway being Microsoft's continued effort to own more of the frontier model stack and offer potentially safer, indemnified models for Microsoft-centric enterprises.

entry.title: Why we Built our own Cloud Agent Infrastructure [ ! ]
entry.summary: Harvey explains why it built its own cloud agent infrastructure for legal AI, emphasizing multi model orchestration, security, zero data retention, and cost control. Our analysts framed this as broadly applicable to regulated industries where AI leaders need more control over data, model routing, infrastructure, and long-term AI automation costs.

entry.title: Anthropic's Browser Agent Got Hijacked 31.5% of the Time Before Safeguards Engaged [ ! ]
entry.summary: The article examines browser-agent prompt injection risk, showing how safeguards can sharply reduce attack success but also how exposed agentic AI systems remain without them. Our analysts emphasized that AI security needs far more attention, especially for APIs, sandboxing, vendor disclosures, and enterprise red-team testing before production deployment.

entry.title: Develop Physical AI Reasoning, World, and Action Models with NVIDIA Cosmos 3 [ * ]
entry.summary: NVIDIA Cosmos 3 is an open physical AI model that combines reasoning, world generation, and action generation for robotics, autonomous systems, and simulation. Our analysts highlighted its open weights, datasets, training recipes, and NIM deployment path as important for advancing Generative AI in the physical world.

entry.title: Powering Agentic AI Sales Strategy with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore [ * ]
entry.summary: This AWS case study describes a Field Advisor system that orchestrates more than 20 specialized sales agents through a single conversational interface. Our analysts viewed it as a useful enterprise pattern for multi-agent coordination, human-in-the-loop workflows, memory, identity, observability, and agentic AI deployment, even though the business-impact metrics were limited.

entry.title: Anthropic Files to Go Public, Setting Stage for Huge I.P.O. [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic confidentially filed for an IPO, signaling another major step in the commercialization of frontier AI and large language models. Our analyst concluded that the news itself is worth knowing, but the article offered little actionable detail beyond market awareness.

entry.title: MiniMax M3 [ ~ ]
entry.summary: MiniMax M3 is an open-weight model positioned around coding, agentic workflows, multimodality, and a long context window. Our analysts noted that it may be worth tracking for cost-sensitive AI automation experiments, but treated it as another product announcement in a crowded open-model market.

entry.title: How Verizon Connect Scaled Agentic AI to 100,000 Users [ * ]
entry.summary: Verizon Connect scaled agentic AI to turn massive vehicle-fleet data streams into actionable insights for users. Our analysts highlighted the impressive scale, cost optimization across models, and broader relevance for companies trying to extract value from IoT and operational data.

entry.title: NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows Puts a Trillion-Parameter AI Supercomputer on Every Enterprise Desk [ * ]
entry.summary: NVIDIA is extending enterprise AI infrastructure to Windows desktops with a desk-side system designed for trillion-parameter AI workloads. Our analysts framed this as strategically important for local AI, AI security, and enterprises that want powerful models without relying entirely on cloud deployment.

entry.title: AI's Impact on SaaS Will Be Uneven. Here's What Leaders Need to Know [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article argues that Generative AI will affect SaaS unevenly depending on data type and whether outputs are deterministic or predictive. Our analysts found the framework useful, but not actionable enough for AI leaders deciding whether to replace or retain major SaaS platforms.

entry.title: Mistral AI Launches Vibe, Expands into Industrial AI And Announces Data Center Push to Challenge OpenAI [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Mistral AI is expanding with Vibe, industrial AI capabilities, and a data center strategy aimed at enterprise and sovereign AI needs. Our analysts noted the strategic importance of verticalization, Europe-focused AI infrastructure, and open-weight models, but rated it optional for most AI leaders outside those contexts.

entry.title: AI Is Already Rewiring the Aftermarket and Services [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article outlines how AI can improve aftermarket sales, service, parts identification, and customer support workflows. Our analysts viewed the topic as relevant for industrial companies, but found the article too general and lacking concrete company-level specifics or economics.

entry.title: Agent Judge: Solving Long Context Evaluations [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Agent Judge addresses long-context evaluation challenges for production AI agents by using more capable evaluation agents rather than one-shot LLM judges. Our analysts agreed the evaluation problem is important, but treated this article mainly as a product announcement rather than a must-read breakthrough.

entry.title: The Cursor Developer Habits Report [ ! ]
entry.summary: This report analyzes how developers are using AI coding tools and shows how AI is changing software development economics, productivity, context usage, and model cost tradeoffs. Our analysts emphasized that context is becoming a critical layer for large language models, with caching, task-level pricing, and developer adoption patterns offering important signals for AI leaders.

entry.title: Narrative Violation: In B2B Customer Support, AI is a Copilot, Not a Replacement [ ! ]
entry.summary: This article uses B2B customer support data to show that AI is functioning more as a copilot and triage layer than a full replacement for human support teams. Our analysts emphasized that customer support is a major Generative AI use case, but the most valuable deployments still require humans in the loop for complex, high-stakes tickets.

entry.title: How Lyft Built a Self-Serve AI Agent Platform for Customer Support with LangGraph and LangSmith [ ! ]
entry.summary: Lyft built a self-serve AI agent platform that lets non-engineers create customer support agents using structured workflows, evaluation, and tracing. Our analysts highlighted this as an essential enterprise AI case study because it shows the importance of semantic layers, prompt structure, observability, and domain-expert involvement in production AI automation.

entry.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.8 [ * ]
entry.summary: Claude Opus 4.8 is an upgraded frontier AI model with improvements in coding, agentic workflows, effort controls, tool use, and safety behavior. Our analysts noted that while the model is stronger and better at flagging uncertainty or flawed code, it remains an incremental upgrade rather than a fundamental shift for most enterprise AI leaders.

entry.title: Gemini Embedding 2: A Native Multimodal Embedding Model from Gemini [ * ]
entry.summary: Gemini Embedding 2 introduces a native multimodal embedding model designed to represent text, images, audio, and other data types in a shared semantic space. Our analysts treated this as an important infrastructure signal because multimodal embeddings could improve retrieval, RAG systems, and future AI model performance, though it is not yet something most AI leaders can immediately operationalize.

entry.title: LFM2.5-8B-A1B: an Even Better on-Device Mixture-of-Experts [ ~ ]
entry.summary: LFM2.5-8B-A1B is an on-device mixture-of-experts model focused on efficient reasoning, instruction following, and reduced hallucinations. Our analysts noted promising technical progress, especially the model's ability to say "I don't know," but rated it optional because real-world edge deployment examples and broad implementation evidence remain limited.

entry.title: Building Self-Improving Tax Agents with Codex [ ! ]
entry.summary: OpenAI and Thrive Holdings built Tax AI for Crete accountants, using Codex, practitioner feedback, production traces, and evals to improve tax-preparation automation. Our analysts viewed this as a strong, generalizable AI automation case study because it shows how domain expertise can be converted into a self-improving agent loop.

entry.title: Choosing to Stay Human [ * ]
entry.summary: This article argues that Generative AI should be used intentionally rather than as a default substitute for human thinking, especially in writing and learning. Our analysts emphasized that AI tutors and workplace tools should challenge users rather than simply provide answers, because cognitive effort remains central to learning and competitive advantage.

entry.title: From Open Source Software to Open Source Strategy [ * ]
entry.summary: This article frames open source as a strategic tool for commoditizing infrastructure, countering platform control, and shaping AI competition. Our analysts saw it as important context for AI leaders, especially around open weights, open AI ecosystems, and the strategic role of shared infrastructure, even though the piece was less immediately actionable.

entry.title: CFOs Funded the AI Revolution. Now They're Joining It [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article discusses how finance organizations are starting to use AI for workflow redesign, analysis, and faster time to value. Our analysts agreed AI in finance is an important trend, but found the article too high-level and lacking the practical "how" needed for CFOs or AI leaders to act on it.

entry.title: Introducing 1-bit and Ternary Bonsai Image 4B: Image Generation for Local Devices [ ~ ]
entry.summary: PrismML introduced compressed 1-bit and ternary versions of Bonsai Image 4B designed to run image generation locally on devices such as iPhones and Macs. Our analysts viewed local AI-driven content creation as important long term, but rated this optional because it is still early and primarily a product announcement.

entry.title: Is a Compute Crunch Coming? [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article examines whether AI inference and training demand could outpace global compute supply. Even though the article sparked a useful debate about token growth, pricing, inference optimization, and chip supply, our analysts rated it optional because its conclusions depended on uncertain assumptions and did not add a crisp action plan.

entry.title: Managers Are Struggling to Keep Up with the AI Productivity Boom [ ! ]
entry.summary: This article explains how Generative AI has accelerated individual output so much that managers are becoming the new bottleneck for review, feedback, and validation. Our analysts framed this as an essential organizational shift: AI productivity only scales when management processes change from traditional oversight to faster validation and decision systems.

entry.title: D&B's Database of 642 Million Businesses Was Built for Humans, Not AI Agents. So They Rebuilt It. [ ! ]
entry.summary: D&B rebuilt its massive commercial data graph so AI agents can query, resolve, and act on business records rather than relying on human-oriented database structures. Our analysts emphasized this as a major AI infrastructure case study: companies must rebuild data foundations, semantic layers, and agent access patterns before AI automation can scale reliably.

entry.title: A Terminal Is All You Need for Web Agents [ * ]
entry.summary: Webwright from Microsoft Research presents a terminal-native approach for web agents, where AI can create reusable scripts, inspect browser sessions, and turn web tasks into repeatable tools. Our analysts highlighted its importance because deterministic code, reusable skills, and better context control could make AI agents more reliable than current browser-clicking approaches.

entry.title: How Glance Turns Hours of Video into Mobile-Ready Clips with AI [ * ]
entry.summary: Glance from Google uses AI to convert long-form video into short, vertical, mobile-ready clips by combining speech-to-text, Gemini-based moment selection, speaker detection, reframing, and captions. Our analysts viewed it as a useful AI-driven content creation case study, especially because it shows how probabilistic AI and deterministic editing tools can work together in production.

entry.title: Introducing Grok Build [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Grok Build is xAI's early beta coding agent and terminal CLI for software development workflows. Our analysts considered it optional because it is mainly a product announcement and catch-up entry in the AI coding agent market, with limited evidence so far on performance or enterprise readiness.

entry.title: Some Ideas for What Comes Next, May 2026 [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This post offers observations on open models, frontier AI systems, product direction, and AI security themes. Our analysts found it to be a useful aggregation of AI news and predictions, but not actionable enough for AI leaders to treat as more than optional reading.

entry.title: How I Choose Which Cloudflare Employees to Replace With AI [ ! ]
entry.summary: Cloudflare's CEO explains a framework for using AI automation to reduce roles in middle management, operations, and measurement-heavy functions while continuing to grow elsewhere. Our analysts emphasized that this gives AI leaders a concrete model for evaluating workforce impact, especially around builders, sellers, and coordinating roles.

entry.title: The Best Manufacturers Build AI with Workers, Not for Them [ * ]
entry.summary: This HBR article argues that manufacturers should involve frontline workers directly in AI adoption rather than treating AI as top-down replacement automation. Our analysts highlighted the importance of leadership involvement, change management, and worker participation as AI anxiety rises across industries.

entry.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills [ * ]
entry.summary: SkillOpt proposes a method for improving agent skills by testing, scoring, and editing skill documents so they perform better across large language models and execution environments. Our analysts emphasized that skills are becoming a critical layer for AI agents, with potential value for transferability, modularity, and avoiding model lock-in.

entry.title: I'm the C.E.O. of Goldman Sachs. The A.I. Job Apocalypse Is Overblown. [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This opinion piece argues that fears of an AI job apocalypse are overstated and that labor markets will adapt as they have before. Our analysts viewed the topic as important but found the argument too light and insufficiently actionable for AI leaders.

entry.title: Adventhealth Advances Whole-Person Care with OpenAI [ ~ ]
entry.summary: AdventHealth is using ChatGPT in healthcare workflows to reduce administrative burden and return time to clinicians and staff. Our analysts considered the healthcare use case relevant but found the case study too high-level and light on implementation detail.

entry.title: How AI Is Forcing McKinsey and Its Peers to Rethink Pricing [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article examines how generative AI may pressure consulting and professional services firms to move away from hourly billing toward fixed-price or outcome-based models. Our analysts noted that pricing pressure is real, but the article added limited new insight because outcome-based pricing has long been difficult to define and measure.

entry.title: An OpenAI Model Has Disproved a Central Conjecture In Discrete Geometry [ ! ]
entry.summary: An OpenAI model helped disprove a long-standing discrete geometry conjecture related to the unit distance problem. Our analysts framed this as a major signal that AI can accelerate discovery by connecting ideas across mathematical and scientific fields to arrive at scientific breakthroughs.

entry.title: Qwen3.7: The Agent Frontier [ ! ]
entry.summary: Qwen3.7-Max is Alibaba's new agentic AI model focused on coding, reasoning, tool use, and long-horizon autonomous workflows. Our analysts emphasized its low-cost frontier positioning and relevance for AI leaders evaluating future model mixes for enterprise AI automation.

entry.title: Presien Reduces Critical Safety Events on Construction Sites by 70%+ with Claude [ ! ]
entry.summary: Presien uses Claude for real-time construction-site safety monitoring, shifting from manual video review to continuous AI-driven risk detection. Our analysts highlighted this case as a strong example of Generative AI moving beyond knowledge work into physical operations, risk reduction, and continuous feedback loops.

entry.title: Meet Stable Audio 3.0, the Model Family Built for Artistic Experimentation with Open-Weight Models [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Stable Audio 3.0 introduces open-weight generative audio models trained on licensed data for music and sound creation. While the licensing and creative AI angle is notable, our analysts concluded that enterprise use cases remain narrow.

entry.title: How Ramp Engineers Accelerate Code Review with Codex [ ~ ]
entry.summary: Ramp is using Codex to speed up code review and support internal developer workflows. Our analysts agreed the topic of AI-assisted engineering bottlenecks is important, but the article itself was light on implementation detail and metrics.

entry.title: Your AI Change Is Actually a People Change [ ~ ]
entry.summary: This article argues that AI transformation depends as much on people, behavior, and change management as on technology. Our analysts acknowledged the importance of the topic but found the guidance too general and not actionable enough for AI leaders.

entry.title: The AI fluency gap between companies [ ! ]
entry.summary: This piece argues that enterprise AI adoption is less about buying tools and more about building institutional fluency, workflow change, and AI-first cultural expectations. The discussion emphasized Zapier as an exemplar: firms with AI-fluent employees can unlock faster prototyping, faster deployment velocity, and broader productivity gains, especially when non-technical teams learn by doing.

entry.title: How DoorDash built an AI code reviewer engineers actually listen to [ ! ]
entry.summary: DoorDash's case study shows how an AI code reviewer can improve pull-request quality by tailoring feedback to company-specific engineering practices and institutional knowledge. The key insight is that useful agentic systems must avoid alert fatigue, earn trust, and automate an organization's "cognitive uniqueness" rather than merely applying generic code-review rules.
